patch_description: Replace the naive concentric-ring layout with a hexagonal lattice layout of 26 circles (alternating rows of 5 and 6 circles, one dropped), which is the known optimal local structure for dense circle packing. Then replace the one-pass pairwise scaling radius computation with an iterative "shrink-to-constraint" growth algorithm: start each radius large and repeatedly shrink each radius to the minimum of (distance to walls) and (distance to each neighbor minus that neighbor's radius). This converges monotonically to a valid packing where most circles touch either walls or neighbors, dramatically increasing the sum of radii (roughly 26 × 0.085 ≈ 2.2, versus the current 0.96).
